text.p: Italian bond futures edged higher ahead of preliminary CPI October data from three Italian cities which were expected to show a fall in average inflation and open the way for a cut in interest rates later this year.
Dealers said the market continue to move higher helped by the positive trend to bunds and T-bonds, and continued optimism over Italy joining the European single currency.

They added that the focus was clearly on data from Milan, Trieste and Turin, the first of ten cities to report October data, with analysts generally looking for a fall in October to a year-on-year 3.2 percent rate from September's 3.4 percent.

The three Italian cities will be followed by seven more on Tuesday, and it is hoped that inflation will continue its fall in October, after it stalled in September from August's 3.4 percent, dealers said.
The figures could open up the possibility of an inflation rate of below three percent in November, a level at which the Bank of Italy has highlighted as leading to a further fall in interest rates.
Dealers added the market largely shrugged off comment by Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher Italy should not take part in the start of the European single currency.
